blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Careers are rarely a straight line. Most professionals today move sideways, across functions and sometimes across countries, before they move up. A career path is a map of possible moves from one role to another. HR designs these paths so people can see where they can go — not just up, but also across the business.

Internal mobility is good for everyone: the employee grows, the manager gains a motivated colleague, and the company keeps valuable knowledge in house. A lateral move is not a step back; it often builds the broader skills that stronger leaders need.

Succession planning is the serious version of this. For every critical role, HR and the business identify one or two successors — people who, with the right development, will be ready to step in when the moment comes. Some are ready now; others will be ready later. The point is that no critical role should depend on a single person.

items.q: According to the text, how do most professionals move before they move up?
options: Out of the company and back
items.why: "Most professionals today move sideways, across functions and sometimes across countries, before they move up."

items.q: Why does HR design career paths?
options: To reduce salaries across the business
So people can see where they can go — up and across
To limit movement to promotions only
items.why: "HR designs these paths so people can see where they can go — not just up, but also across the business."

items.q: What does the text suggest about a lateral move?
options: It is a demotion in disguise
It should be avoided by ambitious people
It can build the broader skills leaders need
items.why: Inferência: "A lateral move is not a step back; it often builds the broader skills that stronger leaders need."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A critical role can safely depend on one irreplaceable person.
Internal mobility benefits the employee and the company.
Some successors are ready now and others later.
Careers are maps rather than straight lines.
items.why: Inferência: o texto conclui que "no critical role should depend on a single person" — o autor discordaria da alternativa oposta.

items.q: The phrase "the serious version of this" suggests that succession planning…
options: is a more formal, higher-stakes form of the same idea
items.why: Inferência: sucessão é apresentada como a forma mais formal e de maior risco da mesma lógica de mobilidade e desenvolvimento.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie conduzindo a reunião de revisão de talentos. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, thanks everyone. Today we're going to work through the top twenty roles, and for each one I want at least one name — ideally two. This isn't a promotion committee; it's a talent review. We're mapping who could step in, and how ready they are.

Let's use the simple frame: ready now, or ready later. If someone is ready now, great — but we still need to keep them visible to the senior team. If they're ready later, tell me what development they need and by when. "Later" without a plan is just a gap we're pretending isn't there.

One thing I'll push on today. Don't only look up. Some of your strongest successors will come from a lateral move — someone from a different function who brings a fresh angle. And please, be honest. If a critical role has no credible successor, I'd rather hear that now than discover it the week someone resigns.

After this meeting, I'm going to share the pipeline with the exec team, and we'll review it again next quarter — not next year.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Sophie ask the leaders to provide for each of the top twenty roles?
options: At least one name, ideally two
items.why: "for each one I want at least one name — ideally two."

items.q: What frame does Sophie ask the group to use?
items.why: "Let's use the simple frame: ready now, or ready later."

items.q: What does Sophie mean by "'Later' without a plan is just a gap we're pretending isn't there"?
options: A successor labelled 'ready later' needs a real development plan, or it is not real cover
The meeting is running out of time
Later successors are always better than ready-now ones
People should never be marked as ready later
items.why: Inferência: sem plano de desenvolvimento, dizer "pronto depois" só disfarça a falta de sucessor.

items.q: Why does Sophie tell the leaders not to "only look up"?
options: Because strong successors can come from a lateral move in another function
Because senior roles are being cut
Because promotions are frozen this year
items.why: "Some of your strongest successors will come from a lateral move — someone from a different function."

items.q: What can we infer about Sophie's attitude to honesty in the review?
options: She sees honesty as less important than speed
She would rather know about a gap now than be surprised later
She wants every role marked as fully covered
She prefers optimistic answers to protect morale
items.why: Inferência: "I'd rather hear that now than discover it the week someone resigns" — prefere a verdade antecipada.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We mapped a clear career path for every analyst on the team." A career path is…
options: a map of possible moves from one role to another
items.why: Career path = trilha de carreira: o mapa dos movimentos possíveis entre funções.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Strong ___ lets us fill roles with people who already know the business."
items.why: Internal mobility = mobilidade interna: aproveitar quem já conhece a empresa.

items.q: "She made a lateral move from finance into operations." A lateral move is…
options: a promotion to a higher grade
a change to a role at a similar level in another area
items.why: Lateral move = movimento lateral: mudar para função de nível parecido, em outra área.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Every ___ must have at least one named successor."
items.why: Critical role = papel crítico: a função essencial que precisa de sucessor identificado.

items.q: "A healthy pipeline means we are never caught short when a leader leaves." Here, pipeline means…
options: a fixed list of open vacancies
a ready supply of future candidates for key roles
items.why: Pipeline (de talentos) = reserva de candidatos prontos para assumir funções-chave.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de talento e sucessão. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "HR asked the exec team to sign off on the succession list." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new career framework team by team." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, por etapas.

items.q: "A manager pushed back on naming only one successor." She…
options: resisted or disagreed with the idea
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar de algo, sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "He was promised development but the plan was never followed through." This means the plan was…
options: not carried through to the end
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, isso não aconteceu.

items.q: "A high-potential analyst needs exposure to leaders to stand out." To stand out means to…
items.why: Stand out = destacar-se, ser claramente notado — ligado à ideia de visibilidade da lição.
